goldens.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
goldens.reasoning: C1 flags the same problem: mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined when destinationCalendar is null or empty.

goldens.comment: The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.
goldens.reasoning: No candidate says the optional chaining is redundant. C1 actually asks for more guarding.

goldens.comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
goldens.reasoning: C2 points to the same flawed fallback lookup (externalId === externalCalendarId), which gives an undefined calendarId. It gets there from a slightly different angle.

goldens.comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
goldens.reasoning: C3 flags the same inverted org slug and requestedSlug logic under IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED.

goldens.comment: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).
goldens.reasoning: C4 says Lark's createEvent signature lacks credentialId and should be updated, which is the same interface mismatch.

goldens.comment: The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.
goldens.reasoning: C5 flags the same risk: credential can be undefined when it is passed to updateEvent.

candidates: mainHostDestinationCalendar can be undefined when evt.destinationCalendar is null/[], accessing .integration will throw and break booking creation/reschedule for Meet location - use optional chaining or a guard

In updateEvent, externalCalendarId can be null/empty (passed from booking references), the current fallback branch searches for externalId === externalCalendarId (which will be null/undefined) and can produce an undefined calendarId, causing the Google API call to fail - provide a reliable fallback

This inverts the org slug behavior compared to the existing publish/update flow - elsewhere when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true and an org isn't published yet, the slug is stored in metadata.requestedSlug (not team.slug) - setting slug directly here under team billing likely bypasses that flow

Same issue as other calendar services: Lark always uses the first element of event.destinationCalendar - for collective/multi-host bookings, EventManager will call createEvent once per destination/credential, without selecting by credentialId Lark event creation for secondary hosts can target the wrong calendar ID - update the signature to accept credentialId and pick the matching destination calendar

If a calendar reference has credentialId but that credential isn't present in this.calendarCredentials and also can't be fetched from DB, credential stays undefined and updateEvent(credential, ...) will throw a non-obvious runtime error - add an explicit guard or return a failure result before calling updateEvent

credentialId is now only set on references when isCalendarType is true, but video references rely on credentialId for later cleanup (cancellation uses bookingVideoReference.credentialId), so dropping it will prevent deleting/updating the created video meeting

selectedCalendar can be undefined when destinationCalendar doesn't contain an entry for the passed credentialId, the insert uses fallback to 'primary' but later events.patch({ calendarId: selectedCalendar }) will be called with undefined and can fail - default selectedCalendar to 'primary' when not found

In deleteEvent, the fallback path tries to find a destinationCalendar entry matching externalCalendarId even when externalCalendarId is falsy, resulting in undefined and relying on later ternaries - simplify and make the fallback explicit to avoid deleting from the wrong calendar

evt.destinationCalendar is set to null when neither event type nor organizer has a destination calendar, but later collective logic appends team members via evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...) - if organizer has no destination calendar, team host destination calendars will be dropped - prefer an empty array so the collective append always works

When dynamicUserList is missing/empty for a dynamic booking, this currently throws a generic Error and gets converted into a 500 'Unable to load users' - that's a client input problem and should return a 400 with a clear message

In the recurring-event branch, the code already iterates all calendar credentials and deletes events for all updatedBookings, when there are multiple _calendar references the surrounding loop will repeat that same work for each reference, causing duplicate delete calls and unnecessary API load - exit the loop after completing the recurring deletion pass
